Edmund Burke, Reflections on the Revolution in France.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/edmund-burke/reflections-on-the-revolution-in-france

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Edmund Burke, the author, the annotator and the writer of the preface, died 1797.

First publication of the text used: 1790 (SE colophon: 'Reflections on the Revolution in France was published in 1790 by Edmund Burke.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the Standard Ebooks rights statement says the text is in the US public domain, and the text was first published in 1790, before 1931, so it is public domain there.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die did so in 1797, so this holds by 1 January 1898.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
